Implementation recommendation: let m_t=1[sequence_t≠0] and x_t=m_t·item_emb(sequence_t). Compute r_t=Σx_j/max(1,Σm_j) over j=max(0,t−4)…t using prefix-sum differences, or left-pad embeddings and masks by four and unfold five-position windows. Explicit mask division handles sequence padding; pooling defaults alone do not. Re-mask padded outputs. Pool item embeddings before positional encoding, documenting any embedding scaling. Fuse z_t=(1−g_t)h_t+g_t r_t with fixed g, learned constant sigmoid(a), or feature-conditioned sigmoid(wᵀ[h_t;r_t]+b); use identical initial gate values. At inference gather the greatest index with sequence≠0, with an explicit empty-history fallback; length−1 fails for left padding. These are proposed controls grounded in [PyTorch pooling semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.AvgPool1d.html).

Ablate baseline versus pooling with added normalization absent, score scale fixed at one, and one negative. Then cross pooling on/off with added LayerNorm, positive learned score scale, and negative count independently; retain baseline SASRec normalization throughout. Compare fixed, learned constant, and conditioned gates; window sizes 1/5; and full-prefix pooling. Match training steps, initialization, optimizer, loss reduction, sampling distribution, and checkpoint selection. Positive global scaling preserves inference ranking but changes training gradients. Negative-count changes require separate attribution: [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) combines increased negatives with a modified loss.

[Original SASRec sampling](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py) excludes full training histories. Without user IDs, sample extra negatives inside the sampler before discarding identity. Alternatively precompute sequence/positive signatures mapped to training-history exclusion sets, handling ambiguous signatures conservatively. Vectorize candidate draws and reject collisions using sorted membership or hash sets; sample complements for dense histories. Visible-sequence filtering alone cannot guarantee full-history exclusion.
